newsitem.title: USA: CFTC settles fraud complaints with trader, broker.
newsitem.headline: CFTC settles fraud complaints with trader, broker.

text.p: The Commodity Futures Trading Commission announced settlement orders with floor trader Craig Effron and floor broker John Gandolfo, both of whom the CFTC accused of cheating customers.
In orders related to an Oct. 19, 1992 complaint, the agency fined each man $100,000 and revoked their CFTC registrations.
The CFTC said in its settlement orders that Effron and Gandolfo participated in non-competitive and fictitious trades at the COMEX and NYMEX.
The agency found Effron violated commodity regulations by helping floor brokers on COMEX and NYMEX in "cheating and defrauding" their customers.
Gandolfo also participated in noncompetitive trades by "bucketing" or trading indirectly opposite his orders to resolve errors he made in handling customers orders.
Both men were prohibited from trading on a contract market for one year, and agreed to cooperate in any related investigations.
CFTC Commissioner John Tull dissented from the agency's settlement with Gandolfo.
Effron and Gandolfo consented to the CFTC settlement without admitting or denying the findings, and agreed to cooperate in any related investigations.
